title: Field-Centric Mecanum Drive

hints.title: What field-centric means
hints.content: In robot-centric drive, pushing the stick forward always drives the robot in the direction the robot faces. In field-centric, pushing forward always drives toward the far end of the field, regardless of which way the robot is rotated. The IMU provides the robot's heading so we can rotate the stick vector to compensate.

hints.title: The rotation formula
hints.content: To rotate a vector (x, y) by angle θ: `rotX = x*cos(θ) - y*sin(θ)` and `rotY = x*sin(θ) + y*cos(θ)`. Use `-heading` because we want to undo the robot's rotation, not add to it.

hints.title: Getting the heading
hints.content: Initialize the IMU in init(), call `imu.resetYaw()` after `waitForStart()`, then read: `double heading = imu.getRobotYawPitchRollAngles().getYaw(AngleUnit.RADIANS);`
